Repo-wide total: 1,223 -> 876 occurrences. Phases 7-14 (purge, territory-disjoint, any order) and Phase 15 (blocking hook flip, strictly last) remain.

decisions_made: check-task-references.sh's PATH_SCOPE argument form: bash check-task-references.sh [--quiet] [PATH_SCOPE]. PATH_SCOPE must fall under (equal to or a subdirectory of) one of the four TREE_ROOTS or the script exits 2. Validated live: agent-system/extensions/core/context reports 147 (matched Phase 4's Scope Hypothesis exactly), unscoped --quiet still reports the identical 1223/563/610/32/18 breakdown as before the amendment.

New Exemption Taxonomy Category 6 (added to rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md during Phase 5, discovered live): 'Test fixtures for the reference-pattern detector itself'. scripts/tests/test-validate-no-task-references.sh and scripts/tests/test-census-count.sh deliberately author literal 'task N' strings as regex-assertion inputs. These are marked with task-ref-ok:begin/end (kept verbatim) rather than converted to {N} placeholders, because a placeholder never satisfies TASK_PATTERN's [0-9]+ requirement and would silently disable the positive-match assertions. This category will matter again in Phase 15 when the same test file is further extended with more fixtures per the plan's own Phase 15 task list -- new fixtures added there should also get this same marker treatment, not be left unmarked.

Phase 6's Scope Hypothesis (84 occurrences) was corrected to 79 in the plan text: Phase 1 actually cleared 5 occurrences from rules/git-workflow.md, not 3, so the 84 figure double-undercounted by 2. Live count matched 79 exactly (skills 25, commands 28, agents 20, rules 1, hooks 3, merge-sources 2) before any Phase 6 edit.

Two recurring citation clusters were each resolved with ONE reused durable-anchor phrase applied identically everywhere they appeared, rather than crafting a bespoke rewrite per site: (a) 'task 796' (mandatory topic-assignment decision) -- 14 occurrences across skill-fix-it, skill-spawn, skill-project-overview SKILL.md files, commands/review.md, commands/task.md, and agents/meta-builder-agent.md -- resolved by simply dropping the citation since the surrounding prose in every instance already stated 'mandatory'/'non-empty by construction' etc. (b) 'task 809'/'task 810' (cross-task file_scope overlap check / a gate-in refactor) -- appeared in near-identical blocks across commands/plan.md, research.md, revise.md -- resolved using 'the cross-task file_scope overlap check' (matching task-lock.md's own established anchor from Phase 4) and 'a gate-in refactor' respectively.

The BimodalLogic 'task-273' baseline (cited in context/contracts/anti-analysis.md and merge-sources/claudemd.md, i.e. the source for CLAUDE.md's own Hard Mode section) was renamed to 'the BimodalLogic per-phase-dispatch baseline' in BOTH locations identically, since it is a cross-repo case-study name, not a citation of a task in THIS repo's tracker, but the same taxonomy applies: no repo-relative task number should appear in a deliverable regardless of which repo it names.

postflight-pattern.md's 8 'Task 326' citations (a specific historical phantom-artifact incident: status updated but artifacts weren't actually created) were all renamed to 'the phantom-artifact incident', a durable anchor introduced once in the Overview and reused consistently through every subsequent citation in that file; the identical incident's citation in workflows/preflight-postflight.md was resolved the same way.

task-breakdown.md's and spawn-agent.md's and planner-agent.md's generic WBS-style 'Task 1.1'/'Task 1'/'Task 2' template placeholders (unrelated to real specs/ task numbers -- they number sub-items within a phase, mirroring but not equal to the real 'Task {P}.{N}' plan-checklist convention) were renamed to 'Step N.N' / 'Item N' respectively to remove the literal collision with TASK_PATTERN while preserving the templates' pedagogical concreteness.

The inline task-ref-ok marker, when needed inside a single markdown table row's cell (rules/artifact-formats.md's placeholder-convention table, and the new Category 6 taxonomy row itself), must be placed INSIDE the last cell before the closing pipe -- appending it after the row's trailing pipe breaks GFM table syntax rather than being silently ignored.

Two named task-description sites (commands/orchestrate.md's cross-batch defense-in-depth passage; skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's init-marker fresh-start comment) were resolved exactly per the plan's own stated preference: the orchestrate.md example was restated without a concrete example (the surrounding prose already conveyed the cross-batch mechanism); the init-marker comment was reduced to the mechanism name alone, applied identically to its sibling occurrence in skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md and to task-lock.sh's own init-marker doc comments (task-lock.sh had 9 total 'task 808'/'task 809'/'task 788' citations, all resolved to the bare mechanism names already established in context/patterns/task-lock.md during Phase 4).

5 pre-existing/expected check-extension-docs.sh drift FAILs from before this dispatch remain (verify-deploy.sh, git-workflow.md, no-task-references-in-deliverables.md pending a deploy; orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh, validate-artifact.sh predating this session). This dispatch's Phases 4-6 edits added MORE source-vs-deployed drift FAILs to the same category (every edited file now differs from its undeployed .claude/ copy) -- this is expected and does not block Phases 7-14, which verify against the source-store script exactly as Phases 4-6 did. A deploy + verify-deploy.sh run remains a Phase-15 precondition, not needed before Phase 7.
dead_ends: permissionDecision deny is not usable for this gate: settings.json permissions.allow contains bare Write and Edit entries, the documented precondition under which deny is ignored. Do not revisit.

agent-system/extensions/core/hooks/tests/test-validate-no-task-references.sh does not exist; the real path is agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-validate-no-task-references.sh, declared under provides.scripts.

root-files/settings.json has no PostToolUse Write|Edit entry for this hook to modify; that registration lives in merge-sources/settings-hooks.json under hooks.PostToolUse. root-files/settings.json has PreToolUse but no Write|Edit matcher for this hook yet.

check-task-references.sh's PATH_SCOPE argument only accepts directory paths, not individual file paths -- passing a single file causes the enum_dir '! -d' check to fire and the script reports [SKIP] + 0 occurrences even when the file has real findings. Always scope verification to a directory (or a whole tree) during the remaining phases; cross-check a single file with plain grep instead.

Do not attempt to research the specific historical task behind every recurring 'task N' citation before converting it -- for citations like 'task 796' or 'task 809' that recur many times with the same descriptive parenthetical already present in surrounding prose, the fast and correct move is simply dropping the number (or reusing an already-established anchor phrase), not investigating the historical task to construct a more elaborate replacement. Only architecture-spec.md (structured entirely around per-task component sections) warranted the more involved component-naming treatment.
